readme_content:
[![DOI](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.82901%2Fnemar.nm000435-blue)](https://doi.org/10.82901/nemar.nm000435)

Human medial temporal lobe iEEG during a visual working memory task (Boran et al.; DANDI 000575)
=================================================================================================

Overview
--------
Intracranial recordings from depth electrodes in the medial temporal lobe (amygdala, hippocampus, entorhinal and
parahippocampal cortex) of patients with drug-resistant epilepsy under invasive monitoring at the University Hospital
Zurich, while they performed a visual working memory (change detection) task: arrays of 1, 2, 4 or 6 coloured
squares were memorised (encoding 0.8 s), held over a delay (retention 0.9 s), and compared with a test array (probe,
2 s; answer "same" or "different"). About 192 trials per session.

This dataset is a BIDS-iEEG representation of the continuous iEEG series ("LFP") that the authors released in NWB:

  Boran E, Hilfiker P, Stieglitz L, Hohenheim J, Klaver P, Sarnthein J (2023). Dataset of human medial temporal
  lobe neurons during a visual working memory task (Version 0.231010.1811). DANDI archive.
  https://doi.org/10.48324/dandi.000575/0.231010.1811 (license CC-BY-4.0)

  Article: Boran E, Hilfiker P, Stieglitz L, Sarnthein J, Klaver P (2022). Persistent neuronal firing in the medial
  temporal lobe supports performance and workload of visual working memory in humans. NeuroImage 254:119123.
  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2022.119123

Please cite both. The same release is on GIN (https://gin.g-node.org/USZ_NCH/Human_MTL_units_visual_WM).
Task files (Presentation): https://www.neurobs.com/ex_files/expt_view?id=285. Example NWB reader from the authors:
https://github.com/janhohenheim/nwb-example.
Funding (DANDI record): Swiss National Science Foundation 204651; The Kavli Foundation 2586.

Contents
--------
11 participants with iEEG (sub-01, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, 12, 13), 12 sessions, 13 recordings
(sub-10 is split in two runs, see below), 24-64 contacts per recording.

  sub-<label>/ses-<n>/ieeg/   BrainVision (.vhdr/.vmrk/.eeg), IEEE float32, microvolts; channels.tsv; ieeg.json;
                              events.tsv; electrodes.tsv (MNI coordinates) + coordsystem.json
  sub-<label>/sub-<label>_scans.tsv  source NWB, recording month, NWB rate attribute, sampling rate used
  sourcedata/dandi-000575/    all 18 NWB files of the release (date masked, see Privacy); they also hold the
                              single-unit spike times and waveforms, which are not converted (see below).
                              sourcedata/sourcedata_provenance.json: DANDI asset id, original DANDI SHA-256 and
                              SHA-256 of the masked copy.

Session labels: ses-01 / ses-02 are the session numbers of the NWB identifier
(Human_MTL_units_visual_WM_subjectXX_sessionYY).
Not in the BIDS signal tree because their NWB file has no continuous series (units and trials only; kept in
sourcedata): sub-02 (ses-01), sub-03 ses-02, sub-11 (ses-01), sub-12 ses-02. sub-02 and sub-11 are therefore not in
participants.tsv. For sub-12 ses-01 the release has two NWB files whose iEEG series are identical (sample check)
and differ only in the rate attribute (obj-1h9ryn9: 0.00025; obj-p4v231: 32000); obj-1h9ryn9 was converted.
In both of these files the iEEG series has 63 columns but only 32 distinct contacts: the series' electrode reference
lists 31 contacts twice (AHL2-AHL8, AL1-AL8, ECL1-ECL8, PHR1-PHR8), and the two columns of each repeated contact are
identical over the whole series (checked sample by sample by the conversion script, which stops otherwise). Each
contact is written once, so sub-12 has 32 channels; the dropped source columns are listed in the conversion report
(conversion_report: dropped_duplicate_cols). The NWB files in sourcedata are unchanged.

Why this is a derivative dataset
--------------------------------
The recordings were made with a Neuralynx ATLAS system (hardware passband 1-8000 Hz, NWB electrodes.filtering). The
authors exported them through FieldTrip MATLAB files; 9 of the 12 sessions (10 of 13 recordings) are at 4 kHz, i.e.
downsampled by the authors (the method is not documented), and sub-10 was concatenated from two parts. The dataset is therefore labelled
DatasetType "derivative". sub-04, sub-07 and sub-13 are at 32 kHz.

Sampling rate: the NWB 'rate' attribute is wrong in most files (please read)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Of the 13 NWB files with a continuous series, 11 store rate = 32000 Hz, one stores 0.00025 (a sample period stored as
a rate; the authors' converter code passes rate=0.00025, i.e. 4 kHz) and one (sub-10) stores explicit timestamps. We set the rate per recording from three independent checks:
  1. the 50 Hz mains peak (Switzerland): its position in cycles/sample gives 4000 Hz for sub-01, 03, 05, 06, 08 (both
     sessions), 09, 10 and 12, and 32000 Hz for sub-04, 07 and 13;
  2. coverage: at the chosen rate each series covers all trial, response and spike times of its NWB file (at 32 kHz
     the 4 kHz series would end long before the task does);
  3. sub-10 stores explicit timestamps with a 0.25 ms step (4 kHz).
The rate used and the rate attribute found are listed for every recording in scans.tsv (sampling_frequency_used,
source_rate_attribute). The conversion script re-checks 1 for every file and stops if the evidence disagrees.

Amplitude unit: the NWB says unit "volts" with conversion 1, but the stored numbers are microvolts (median channel
SD 4-60 for the 4 kHz series; the authors' converter writes the FieldTrip matrix unscaled while it scales the spike
waveforms from microvolts by 1e-6). We wrote the stored values as microvolts, unchanged apart from float32 rounding.
No filtering, resampling, re-referencing or cropping was done by this conversion; the only channel change is the
removal of the exact duplicate columns of sub-12 described above.

sub-10: the NWB timestamps restart once (sample 2,013,312: from 503.33 s back to 26.48 s). The authors' converter
joined two recording parts with an offset taken from the trial log and a hand-copied lag; the result is not monotonic,
so the true position of part 2 on the task clock is unknown. Part 1 is run-1 (with the 71 trials that fall inside it,
plus their epochs and responses); part 2 is run-2, without events. All trials remain in the NWB file in sourcedata.

sub-12 ses-01: the 4 kHz series lasts 2806 s, longer than the 191 trials of this file (last trial ends at 1406 s);
the release does not say what the remaining part contains (the ses-02 trials are in a separate NWB without iEEG and
we did not assume a common clock).

Channels and electrodes
-----------------------
Channel names are the authors' contact labels (e.g. AHL1-AHL8 = left anterior hippocampus electrode, contacts 1-8;
AL/AR amygdala, ECL/ECR entorhinal cortex, PHL/PHR parahippocampal cortex). Reference: "Common intracranial
reference" (NWB). channels.tsv/electrodes.tsv column soz = contact inside the seizure onset zone (NWB
is_inside_soz). electrodes.tsv: MNI coordinates (mm) and the authors' Brainnetome anatomical label. The NWB stores
the coordinates in the NWB axis convention (x = -MNI y, y = -MNI z, z = MNI x, as written in the authors' converter);
we converted them back. The MNI template is not specified in the release (coordsystem "Other").

Events
------
events.tsv rows: trial (start to end of each trial; set_size; solution same/different), the trial periods fixation,
memory (encoding), retention and probe (intervals/epochs), and response (button press: same/different). onset is the
NWB time minus the time of the first sample of the series. source_table/source_row_id point back to the NWB.

Not converted
-------------
Single units (spike times, mean/SD waveforms, observation intervals) are in the NWB files in sourcedata/ unchanged; no
BIDS derivative was made from them.

Same participants in other public releases
------------------------------------------
The authors' conversion metadata (https://github.com/janhohenheim/usz-neuro-conversion, in/metadata/participants.csv)
links 7 participants of this release to their verbal working memory release (GIN; NEMAR nm000363, OpenNeuro
ds004752) and/or the fear-video release (OpenNeuro ds003374 / DANDI 000576). See participants.tsv
same_participant_in. These are different tasks and different recordings; no data are duplicated.

Privacy (review 2026-10-08)
---------------------------
All string attributes and datasets of the 18 NWB files were listed. They contain: subject numbers, age, sex,
handedness, pathology, electrode lists, contact labels, anatomical labels, institution/lab, the experimenter (author),
the task description and the session start date-times. The session dates are real recording dates, so: in the
sourcedata copies the day of session_start_time and timestamps_reference_time is set to 01 (year, month and time of
day kept), and the dates in the file names are masked the same way; BIDS files carry only the recording month
(scans.tsv). No names, birth dates or hospital IDs were found in the NWB files. The authors' public conversion
repository holds hospital patient numbers; the hospital therefore keeps a key, and none of those numbers is copied here.

## Ethics

Verbatim from Boran E, Hilfiker P, Stieglitz L, Sarnthein J, Klaver P (2022). Persistent neuronal firing in the medial temporal lobe supports performance and workload of visual working memory in humans. NeuroImage 254:119123. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2022.119123, section "Ethics statement":

> The study was approved by the institutional ethics review board (Kantonale Ethikkommission Zürich, PB-2016-02055) and all participants gave written informed consent.
